notes: setup is the cbr post-install configurator: it idempotently merges the harness settings a plugin cannot ship (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, teammateMode=in-process, worktree.baseRef=head) into the user's .claude/settings.json, and on opt-in installs the enforce-worktree.py base-branch gate and persists the worktree-isolation policy. Evaluate scope choice, the shown-then-applied idempotent merge (no clobbering unrelated keys), and honest reporting of what changed vs was already correct.

evals.prompt: I just installed the cbr plugin — run the ClaudeBrew setup to finish configuring it.
evals.expected_output: Chooses scope (defaults to user ~/.claude/settings.json, offers project), reads current settings, shows the exact keys to add (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, teammateMode=in-process, worktree.baseRef=head) as a diff, deep-merges them idempotently without touching unrelated keys, offers the opt-in worktree gate + policy persistence, and confirms what changed vs was already correct, noting env vars take effect next session.

evals.prompt: Teammate mode isn't working in cbr brainstorming and my worktrees keep branching from the wrong base — can you fix the cbr config?
evals.expected_output: Triggers setup, reads the target settings, verifies/merges the agent-teams env var, teammateMode=in-process, and worktree.baseRef=head, reports which were missing vs already correct, and reminds the user that the env-var change takes effect on the next Claude Code session.

evals.prompt: Allow npm commands in my project settings and set DEBUG=true.
evals.expected_output: A generic .claude/settings.json change unrelated to the cbr harness; should NOT trigger cbr setup. Routes to update-config (the settings.json specialist that setup itself names as its delegate) — setup only manages the specific cbr harness keys.
